page: Microsoft Azure D96plds_v6 is an arm64 instance powered by 96 dedicated cores of Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 silicon clocked at 3.4 GHz. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the architecture supplies one thread per physical core with 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 128 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory allocation totals 192 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes 5670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It features hardware AES cryptographic support but does not include discrete GPUs.

Performance profiles demonstrate top-tier execution across heavily parallel tasks. In multi-threaded compute benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier scores in stress-ng multi-core testing and Geekbench multi-core processing, alongside strong marks in Clang software compilation and ray tracing. Memory throughput is substantial, measuring 464.56 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 205.51 GB/sec for writes. Single-core performance across stress-ng and Geekbench registers in the average bracket. I/O-intensive and concurrent tasks excel, evidenced by 170.06 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 102.9 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation creates an architecture favoring compute density over large per-core memory footprints, making it cost-efficient for parallel scale-out workloads without paying for surplus RAM. The integration of 5.67 TB of fast local NVMe storage reduces storage overhead for ephemeral data. Tradeoffs include moderate single-thread speed and the lack of AVX or GPU acceleration. This profile aligns well with software compilation pipelines, large-scale Redis caching, static web hosting clusters, high-concurrency database operations, and multi-threaded data transformations.
description: Microsoft Azure D96plds_v6 is an arm64 server featuring 96 dedicated ARM Neoverse-N2 cores operating at 3.4 GHz with a single thread per core. Configured with 192 GB of memory, it maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside 5670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and no discrete GPUs. The instance exhibits top-tier multi-core computing capability, demonstrating high benchmark ratings in Clang compilation, ray tracing, and stress-ng multi-core tests. High memory bandwidth reaching 464.56 GB/sec read speeds complements notable throughput in Redis key-value workloads and static web serving. While single-thread performance is moderate and per-core RAM is low, the dense core count and bundled fast local storage provide high compute density. Microsoft Azure D96plds_v6 is suited for multi-threaded build farms, distributed caching clusters, high-throughput web frontends, and database engines requiring fast local NVMe scratch space.
